title: Cluster 02 DRILL: Cell and Nuclear Division
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 3 · 7 questions · 90 marks · 20 parts · one mark per minute, so 90 minutes · cumulative over Book 3 Cluster 1 and Books 1 and 2
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Seven questions, 90 marks, 90 minutes. Every learning outcome this cluster owns is still tested; the table below shows which question carries each one. The set used to run 103 marks. The saving came from putting checkpoint dysregulation on the same flow-cytometry stem that already deduces the arrest, and from folding the roles of the mitotic cell cycle into the essay that already argues for accurate distribution. No outcome was dropped to make the time.

Six real figures, four questions figure-led. Chapter 3.2 is the most graph-driven chapter in Book 3 at 44.1% figure-led, and data and figure interpretation is 33.5% of Book 3 as a whole. Every figure is the real image from the paper the question came from, not a redrawing.

One MCQ only, and it is the specimen's own. Q5(a) is 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 17 word for word. You have to judge all four statements and all four options, not pick a letter.

Cumulative, and that is the point. Book 2 taught you what meiotic error causes; Book 3 teaches the event, so the two only make sense held together. Q1(a) needs the three-level packing ladder. Q3(c) needs non-disjunction defined and then applied at both anaphases. Q4(c) needs the centromere in Book 2's own words for non-coding DNA. Q5(d) needs unequal crossing over. Q7(b) cannot be written without semi-conservative replication, proofreading and gene mutation. Q7(a) needs the receptor tyrosine kinase and the phosphorylation cascade said cold from Cluster 1. A Book 1 or Book 2 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Cluster 2 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. Name the exact stage at which each event happens; an examiner report in this file calls vague-across-stages description the commonest failure. Write non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes in full. State both sides of every comparison positively, because schemes reject yes-or-no comparisons twice over. Keep the centromere dividing apart from the kinetochore microtubules shortening. Say cell division, never cell growth, whenever the word uncontrolled is in play. Quote figures off any graph you are told to refer to.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicates. Q1 stage identification off a micrograph, and the condensation that makes it readable · Q2 reading a stage off quantitative spindle data, and separation held apart from movement · Q3 the cell cycle read from DNA content, checkpoint arrest and what its failure costs · Q4 non-coding DNA at the chromosome ends and at the centromere · Q5 the sources of genetic variation in meiosis · Q6 mitosis against meiosis in chromosome behaviour, and reduction · Q7 signalling into division, and accuracy of inheritance set against the origin of variation. No concept is the primary target of two questions.

Nothing from Books 4 to 9, and nothing from Book 3 chapter 3.4. Stem cells are not studied yet, so no question needs them. Q3(b) goes exactly as far as LO 2(o) goes and stops.
